versions.name: RXV2-0.9.409-fw-note
versions.notes: New-helicopter checklist gains step 1: a note that a fresh flight controller already has Rotorflight on it (fine to fly), and that installing the very latest firmware first is a one-time USB job with the Rotorflight Configurator on a computer - flashing cannot be done from the phone. A desktop wizard that flashes too is planned.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.408-new-heli
versions.notes: The NEW HELICOPTER wizard begins: a step-by-step from-scratch setup checklist (blades off!) plus the new First-time basics page - level calibration (accelerometer), governor/telemetry/ESC-sensor features, ESC protocol + motor poles + gear ratios, ESC telemetry brand, battery cells/capacity/voltage sources, and one-tap standard channel order (AERCT123). All writes verified by read-back; restart-to-apply handled in-page.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.407-arm-self-taught
versions.notes: Rotorflight takes over Fly now completely: the receiver reads the ARM switch channel straight from the flight controller (MSP mode ranges) - no setup needed. Fly now then hides itself and the arming switch does it all: arm = radios off (3 s, on the ground), disarm = radios back. A manually set arming channel still wins; non-Rotorflight models are unchanged.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.406-arm-cycle
versions.notes: Automatic fly mode, full cycle: radios switch OFF by themselves 3 s after ARMING (on the ground, during spool-up - never mid-air) and back ON when you DISARM. Only WiFi/Bluetooth are touched; the RC link and flight-controller output never stop. With an arming channel set, the front-page Fly now button hides itself - it is no longer needed (models without arming keep it).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.404-auto-fly
versions.notes: NEW: Automatic fly mode (Receiver settings, ON by default) - for everyone who forgets Fly now. When the model is armed and the sticks have been moving for 5 seconds, the receiver switches WiFi and Bluetooth off by itself so nothing interferes with the radio link; everything returns automatically after landing. Needs the arming channel set.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.403-add-picker
versions.notes: Switches page: 'Add a switch action' now first asks WHAT the switch should do (a drop-down of all the functions), then creates the row with that choice ready.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.402-drag-handles
versions.notes: Switches page polish: the blue zone's round ends can now be DRAGGED with a finger to set the range (numbers follow along, snapped to 5 µs), and the live channel marker is a slim red line (green inside the zone).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.401-range-bars
versions.notes: Switches page: each row now shows the configurator-style range bar - the blue zone is where the function is ON, and a LIVE dot shows the channel's actual position (green when inside the zone). Flick a switch and watch it work.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.400-rf-steps
versions.notes: Switches + Rescue-switch card: ranges now decode with Rotorflight's own encoding (signed 5 µs steps about 1500 - range 875-2125), fixing impossible values like ARM showing 3900 µs. Thanks to Malcolm's sharp eye.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.399-single-back
versions.notes: Fixed the twin 'Back to Rotorflight' buttons on the Rotorflight pages - each page keeps exactly one.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.398-modes
versions.notes: NEW: Switches page (Rotorflight menu) - what each transmitter switch makes the flight controller do (Rotorflight's Modes tab, in plain English). See, change, add and remove switch actions - Arm, Rescue, self-level, governor and more - each save verified. The Rescue page's switch card now links straight to the right row here.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.397-rescue-switch
versions.notes: Rescue screen now shows WHICH transmitter channel triggers rescue (read from the flight controller's Modes table), with the active range - and a loud warning if NO switch is assigned, because then rescue can never fire (Malcolm: 'it's critical').
